title: The Orion Bar region (Hubble image)
caption: The Orion Bar region of the Orion Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: [BOM2000] d203-506, HH 520, Messier 42, Orion Bar, Orion Nebula · constellation Orion · about 1400 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Robberto (Space Telescope Science Institute/ESA) and the Hubble Space Telescope Orion Treasury Project Team

recognition.text: Official ESA/Webb press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two large, bright stars sit at the bottom right of this cloudy scene in the Orion Nebula. Toward the top left, the material is dull, thick and smoky. A brighter purple wall cuts across the bottom right, and beyond it the gas becomes wispier and thinner.

The two stars belong to a cluster called θ² Orionis. The Trapezium Cluster of four hot, massive stars, lies just out of view beyond the top-left corner, and it illuminates the gas seen here. Several proplyds, discs of material around young stars, can be spotted among the clouds.

This view is cut from a larger Hubble mosaic covering the whole Orion Nebula, released in 2006. It has been cropped and aligned to match the same area as observed by the James Webb Space Telescope's NIRCam, so the two telescopes' views can be compared directly.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.08 x 2.31 arcminutes) and distance (1400 light years), the frame spans roughly 0.8 × 0.9 light-years. Its light set out about 1,400 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed the region through five filters. Light at 435 nm is shown in blue, 555 nm in green, hydrogen-alpha and nitrogen light at 658 nm in orange, and 775 and 850 nm in red.
understand.eye: The 658 nm filter isolates the glow of specific gases, and Hubble's sharp view shows fine structure such as the proplyds.
